This application coming on for admission this day, the court  passed the following:
 ORDER Vide this common order MCRC No.19859/2016 and MCRC No.1279/2017 are being disposed of.
Since common questions of law and facts are invoked, therefore the facts are being culled out from MCRC No.19859/2016.

2. Petitioner Subhash Chandra Choudhary in MCRC No.19859/2016 has preferred this petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashing of proceedings in Criminal Complaint No.386 of 2016 pending in the Court of Judicial Magistrate First Class, Vijayraghavgarh, District Katni and for setting aside the order dated 27.7.2016 passed by the Judicial Magistrate First Class Vijayraghavgarh, District Katni, securing his presence through bailable warrant for the alleged contraventions of provisions of Sections 7A(2)(a) and 7A(2)(c) of the Factories Act, 1948 (for brevity "Act, 1948") and Rule 73-E of the Madhya Pradesh Factories Rules.

sentences.text:
3. The petitioner is a Factory Manager and Senior General Manager (Plant Operations), ACC Ltd.,
Kymore Cement Works, Kymore, District Katni.
On 30.4.2016 at about 11:00 AM, an activity of clearing a Jam in the Coal Crusher in ACC Plant was being carried out after obtaining all the necessary permits and following the lock-out procedure.
After clearing the crusher, the permit was duly returned and restart of the crusher was attempted.
During the said process of restarting the crusher, siren was also blown for indicating that the crusher is being started.
Deceased Mohd. Hussain, who was an employee of the contractor was given the task of observing the restart process from a safe distance of atleast two meters.
Thereafter the deceased shouted and when other persons rushed to the spot, the deceased was found lying down.
A crowbar was also found next to him.
The deceased was found lying on the floor with an injury on his head, just above the left ear.
Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) including the helmet and eye- goggles were found along with the crowbar near the body of the deceased.

It was summarized that against the clear instructions and past training, the deceased had tried to insert the crowbar in the inspection window of the crusher and the other end of the crowbar hit the workman on the area between the helmet and the ear.
The workman succumbed to his injuries on reaching hospital.
4. The petitioner being Manager and Director of the Plant submitted his personal report on Form No.22 to the Deputy Director of the Industrial Health & Safety, mentioning the accident to be fatal.
The injury was probably caused by the crowbar and the same was on the head over the left ear.
The Factory Inspector i.e. Deputy Director of the Industrial Health & Safety conducted his inspection after visiting the Plant.

As per his report, the deceased was clearing the Jam in the crusher using an Subhash Chandra Choudhary vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190631712/
2 iron rod when suddenly the machine started which caused the rod to strike at his head.

sentences.text: As per the report, the violation was also found.

The Factory Inspector found that the permit was returned before the work had actually completed and it was a case of non-implementation of work permit,
thereby violating the provisions of Section 7A(2)(a) of the Act, 1948 in terms of not ensuring proper safety of the workers.
The crusher had two small windows, which were left open and the work of cleaning the Jam by inserting the iron rod was done by the deceased.
Since the work permit had prematurely been returned and the machine restarted, therefore it amounted to violation of Rule 73-E of the M.P. Factory Rules.

The Factory Inspector also observed that there was no proper supervision when the deceased workman was working and therefore, it was an act of violating the provisions of Section 7A(2)
(c) of the Act, 1948.

( d) the maintenance of all places of work in the factory in a condition that is safe and without risks to health and the provision and maintenance of such means of access to, and egress from, such places as are safe and without such risks;
(e) the provision, maintenance or monitoring of such working environment in the factory for the workers that is safe, without risks to health and adequate as regards facilities and arrangements for their welfare at work."
5 . The petitioner was given a show cause notice to which he had replied by submitting the work permit, energy isolation and lock-out permits.
The said permits were requested by Rajkumar Mishra and issued by Shubham Tiwari, whose statements were also recorded during the inspection conducted by the Factory Inspector.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the report of the Factory Inspector is per se illegal.
The lock after completion of work was to be opened.
The work permit was returned by the deceased worker after completion of work.
Window used to remain open.

Learned counsel for the petitioner vehemently submitted that as per the ACC Limited Occupational Health & Safety Standard for isolation and Lockout, the provision has been made in respect of work permit process i.e. para 3.5.2 of the aforesaid Standard for isolation and Lockout, which prescribes the following characteristics:-
"3.5.2 Work Permit Process i) Work on the equipment (where multiple isolation is carried out to protect single or multiple workers), is permitted after obtaining a written authorization in the form of a work permit.
ii) Permit holder is responsible to initiate and complete the process of isolation and lock out.
iii) Permit shall shall be issued in duplicate with colour code as follows:
i) Pink- for Permit holder- to be displayed at work site.

entities.text: ACC Limited Occupational Health & Safety Standard
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: ii) White- for Permit issuer/CCR.
(pink copy to be kept as record by permit holder & white copy to be kept as record by permit issuer/CCR)

iv) Follow the 12 steps given in section 3.5.1.2 (Process for group isolation-multiple isolation carried out to protect single or multiple workers)
v) Name of all the people working in on the equipment has to be mentioned in the permit at the start of every shift.
vi) Permit issuer & isolation officer shall maintain the necessary permit & register records respectively.
vii) Isolation officers and permit issuers shall be nominated by director plant/ Unit head.
The list of the authorized work permit issuer and isolation officers shall be documented and communicated to all concerned.
viii) I may happen that a permit is issued and after the isolation (LOTO) is done, equipment is required to be sent outside/kept isolated for want of spares or any other services.
a) In this case 'out of order' tag shall be displayed on the relevant equipments/panels/isolation area.

sentences.text: However all the conditions for the safety purpose shall be verified after every handover and takeover by permit holders of shifts.

ix) In case of any emergency in the plant other than the department/location in which work is carried out following protocols shall be adhere:
d) If there is an evacuation of the plant the work shall be stopped after the necessary precautions.

Once the situation is restored to normal and emergency called off, the working conditions shall be verified by the Permit issuer and Permit holder jointly and shall make the comments of the verification on the permit along with their signatures.

e) In case no evacuation is required of the entire plant and emergency is restricted to the related department, the Permit Issuer and Permit holder jointly shall assess for any impact of the emergency on the activity carried out under the permit.
If there is no impact, the permit shall be progressed as in normal condition.
x) In case a personal lock is placed and the concerned lock holder is not available.
This should be considered an offence to leave site with your personal isolation tag in place.
Contact should be made with the person and they should return to site to remove their tag.
Consequence management then applies.
This area of the procedure requires work in linking to cardinal rule 1.

If the concerned person is not available and the lock has to be removed then permit issuer shall obtain an approval from the operations in-charge and operations in-charge should come to the site to ensure that concerned person is safe before authorizing breaking up of such personal lock.

Such approval may be sought in exceptional cases only and must be recorded by the concerned isolation officer."
7.

In the reply to the aforesaid notice, the petitioner submitted detailed reply setting forth the events that transpired on 30.4.2016 i.e. the day of incident and denied his role and contravention of any provisions of the Act,
1948.

(i) That the persons assigned with the responsibility of the jam-clearing activity at the Coal Handling Plant followed ACC's standard operating procedure of Work Permit and Electrical Isolation and only then commenced the jam- cleaning activity;

9. A bare perusal of the aforesaid order would indicate that the same besides being totally non-speaking does not correspond to reasons.
A cryptic type order has been passed without adhering to the prosecution allegations and forming of prima facie opinion by the Court on the basis of material available before it.
Criminal law cannot be set into motion as a matter of course.
The summoning of an accused in a criminal case is a serious matter.
The order of the Magistrate summoning the accused must reflect due application of mind to the facts of the case and the law applicable thereto.
Perusal of the impugned order would indicate that the Court was even not alive to the factual position of the case.

The order of the Magistrate, summoning the accused-petitioner must indicate that he has applied his mind to the facts of the case and the law applicable thereto by examining the nature of allegations made against the petitioner in the complaint and prima-facie evidence brought on record in support of the allegations.

The Court has to scrutinize the evidence brought on record carefully and may even himself put questions to the complainant and witnesses in order to elicit answer to find out the truthfulness of the allegations or otherwise.

In this regard reference can be made to the Pepsi Foods Ltd. and another Vs. Special Judicial Magistrate and others, (1998) 5 SCC 749= 1997(4)
RCR (Criminal) 761.

sentences.text: The Magistrate has to find out as to whether prima facie case exists for summoning of the accused or not.
There is a difference between an accident and violation of rules.
Even after due compliance of the rule, the accident may happen.
The Court is required to ensure existence of prima facie case for the purpose of summoning an accused.

10. After perusal of the impugned order, this Court finds that the same is totally non-speaking,
therefore this Court deems it appropriate to quash the same and remand the case to the Court of concerned Judicial Magistrate First Class with a direction to revisit the issue and record prima facie satisfaction based on the allegations in the complaint and material available on record for the purpose of summoning of the petitioner in accordance with law.

The summoning order must show that the Magistrate has applied his mind to the facts of the case and law applicable thereto after Subhash Chandra Choudhary vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190631712/

For the reasons recorded hereinabove and without observing anything on merits of the case, I deem it appropriate to quash the impugned order and remand the matter back to the concerned Judicial Magistrate First Class with a direction to revisit the issue and pass appropriate order afresh in accordance with law on the basis of parameters as laid down in Pepsi Foods Ltd.
(supra).
12.
Accordingly, the instant petition filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. stands disposed of.
